newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty firms vs basket on Polish paper purchases.
newsitem.headline: Zloty firms vs basket on Polish paper purchases.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed stronger against the basket despite the dollar's surge against the mark, fuelled by large foreign currency sales, likely connected with foreign purchases of Polish T-bills, dealers said.
They said some foreign buyers were also buying Polish paper on the secondary bond market.

"The large sales of currencies might have been caused by foreigners, who became very active after the long weekend on the primary T-bill market and on the secondary bond market," said Marcin Trzykowski from PKO SA.
The zloty closed up at 2.16/2.09 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's 2.14/2.08 percent from parity.
It closed at 2.7970/90 to the dollar, up from 2.8090/05 on Friday and at 1.8690/00 to the mark, down from 1.8607/15.
Investors bid for 753 million zlotys of Polish T-bills at Tuesday's 1.2 billion zloty primary tender.
The zloty was seen weakening tomorow if today's support from foreign currency sales did not spill over to Wednesday, dealers said.
They expected the central bank to fix the zloty relatively high against the dollar during Tuesday's fixing session.
Minimum prices of all Polish T-bills fell 0.01 point at today's primary auction on total demand of 753 million zlotys against a 1.2 billion zloty offer.
The average yield of the shortest 8-week paper rose 0.05 point to 18.60 percent, average yield of 26-week paper rose 0.03 point to 19.21 percent.

The average yield of the longest 52-week paper remained flat at 19.50 percent, but there were players who accepted a fall in the minimum yield to 19.08 percent from 19.40 percent at the last primary tender on November 4, 1996.
